extracted.intended_audience: individual authors (nonfiction humanities writers) preparing NEH Public Scholars grant applications
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and submitting an application to the NEH Public Scholars program, which funds individual authors to research and write well-researched nonfiction humanities books for a broad public. Includes eligibility, budget/duration limits, required application materials, submission procedures, and reviewer-facing guidance resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target work: well-researched nonfiction books for the broad public
rubrics_metrics.description: The Public Scholars program offers grants to individual authors for research, writing, travel, and other activities leading to the creation and publication of well-researched nonfiction books in the humanities written for the broad public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications should propose a humanities nonfiction book intended for a broad public audience; use funds for the research/writing/travel/activities that directly support producing and publishing that book. Sample funded projects (listed on the page) illustrate the kinds of book-length work supported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: individual applicants; no advanced degree required
rubrics_metrics.description: Writers with or without an academic affiliation may apply, and no advanced degree is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program encourages non-academic writers to deepen engagement with the humanities by strengthening research underlying their books, and encourages academic writers to communicate the significance of their research to the broadest possible range of readers. NEH especially encourages applications from independent writers, researchers, scholars, and journalists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding amount and period constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Maximum award amount: $5,000 per month. Period of performance: Six to twelve months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The grant is a monthly stipend up to the stated maximum and must cover a project period within the 6–12 month window. Project start dates are indicated (e.g., September 1, 2025 and September 1, 2026) and applicants should plan schedules to align with those start windows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expected output: book-length publication
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The application should propose work that will result in a book (humanities nonfiction) by the end of the funded period; sample application narratives and previously funded project descriptions can be used to judge appropriate scope and scale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted uses of funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Funds may be used for research, writing, travel, and other activities leading to the creation and publication of the book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget and workplan should tie expenditures directly to project activities (research, archival travel, writing time, etc.) that enable completion and publication of the proposed book.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) and program instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Read the Notice of Funding Opportunity to ensure you understand all the expectations and restrictions for projects delivered under this program and are prepared to write the most effective application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the instructions outlined in the NOFO and Grants.gov instructions exactly when assembling the application package. The page links to the Public Scholars NOFO, Grants.gov application package, FAQs, and sample application narratives as authoritative guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grants.gov registration and applicant profile requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Register for a Grants.gov account and add an 'individual applicant' profile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Click 'My Account' → 'Manage Profiles' → 'Add Profile' to add an individual applicant profile; refer to Grants.gov’s instructions for adding a profile. Ensure your Grants.gov account is current before applying. Download Adobe Reader and follow provided 'Tips for making PDFs.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Application submission and confirmation procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit your application package on Grants.gov; you will receive up to five e-mail messages confirming receipt and different stages in the application acceptance process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify you have received all confirmation messages (they may go to spam/junk). After the final confirmation (the fifth message) NEH will have received the application and you can proceed to monitor recommendation letters; keep Grants.gov tracking number for checking status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of recommendation solicitation and monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Program staff will request letters of reference from your recommenders on or about January 9 (about one month after the application deadline). You will be notified by e-mail when each of your letters of reference has been received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After receipt of the fifth Grants.gov confirmation you may check the status of letters by logging into NEH’s secure area with your NEH application number and Grants.gov tracking number. You will be able to see the names and e-mail addresses of your letter writers and whether their letters have arrived. If necessary, you may send reminders to your letter writers (including the upload link). You are responsible for ensuring that your letter writers have received the solicitations and submitted their letters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use program resources and sample narratives to craft effective applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Program Resources include the Public Scholar Frequently Asked Questions, list of recently funded projects, and sample application narratives (titles provided).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Watch the recorded online information session (30-minute presentation + 30-minute Q&A) that explains goals of the program, eligibility, how to apply, how applications are reviewed, and how to write an effective application. Use sample narratives as models for scope, structure, and level of detail expected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program priority: Humanities Perspectives on Artificial Intelligence initiative
rubrics_metrics.description: This grant program is one of ten NEH programs that are part of NEH’s Humanities Perspectives on Artificial Intelligence initiative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The initiative encourages research on the ethical, legal, and societal implications of AI. Applicants whose projects address these themes may find additional relevance to NEH priorities; see the AI initiative page for more information.
